1	# STDO Toolchain Manager Design
     2	
     3	- Status: active
     4	- Implements: `.ai-workspace/tickets/completed/T-013-create-stdo-toolchain-manager.md`,
     5	  `.ai-workspace/tickets/completed/T-014-make-version-line-selector-latest.md`,
     6	  `.ai-workspace/tickets/completed/T-020-consolidate-specification-stack-monorepo.md`,
     7	  `.ai-workspace/tickets/completed/T-021-qualify-monorepo-release-refs.md`
     8	- Derives from: `specification/PRODUCT.md#product-definition-overlay`
     9	- Supersedes: none
    10	- Superseded by: none
    11	
    12	## Boundary
    13	
    14	The manager is a dependency-light Python command-line application installed
    15	once per user or build image. It manages exact STDO distribution bytes and
    16	Product Definition routing. It does not evaluate semantic conformance, govern a
    17	consumer workflow, infer product composition, or own a consumer's selection.
    18	
    19	The Product Definition is the sole authored selection surface. Its exact basis
    20	is an immutable logical release URI plus the SHA-256 of a deterministic
    21	installed-release manifest. Its version-line selector is discovery input for
    22	the highest-ordinal published immutable RC only.
    23	
    24	## Legacy Installer Disposition
    25	
    26	ABIogenesis `gen-install.py` supplied three useful precedents: an explicit
    27	verify-only path, idempotent marker-delimited `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` updates,
    28	and machine-readable install results. The manager retains those properties.
    29	
    30	It intentionally does not retain that installer's adjacent mutable-source copy,
    31	wholesale `.genesis` replacement, fixed project scaffold, or presence-only
    32	standards verification. Those behaviors coupled method upgrades to one source
    33	checkout and rewrote every consumer. The replacement installs immutable cuts in
    34	one shared store and lets each layout-neutral Product Definition select its own
    35	exact basis.
    36	
    37	## Components
    38	
    39	- `git_source.py` reacquires one annotated immutable RC tag into an isolated
    40	  temporary bare object store and resolves a mutable version-line alias only
    41	  when it matches the highest-ordinal published immutable RC. During the
    42	  shared-source transition it conserves historical unqualified cuts and
    43	  resolves future `specification_methodology/` qualified tags to the unchanged
    44	  product-local cut and public `stdo:` URI. Additional refs to the same exact
    45	  tag object are conserved; equal local cuts naming different tag objects are
    46	  ambiguous and refuse. Channel resolution selects the qualified successor;
    47	  direct logical-cut reacquisition keeps the historical ref when an identical
    48	  preserving alias also exists, so an installed historical manifest does not
    49	  drift. A cut contains
    50	  STDO either at the historical repository root or at the exact monorepo prefix
    51	  `specification_methodology/`, never both. Physical nested paths are projected
    52	  back to project-relative logical source paths before manifest construction.
    53	- `manifest.py` derives the exact tag, commit, trees, standards inventory,
    54	  canonical member-set digest, member bytes, license, release note, and plugin
    55	  payload admitted to an installation. A qualified shared-source cut also
    56	  retains its Project Release Namespace, qualified ref, Project Subtree root,
    57	  and Project Subtree tree; historical manifests remain byte-reproducible.
    58	- `store.py` atomically materializes immutable cuts, records logical URI
    59	  mappings, resolves members within the release root, and detects missing,
    60	  extra, changed, or redirected state.
    61	- `product_definition.py` discovers overlays, validates them against their
    62	  exact schema, reports and synchronizes pinned bases, performs explicit
    63	  selector adoption, and updates marker-bounded agent bootstraps.
    64	- `cli.py` exposes singular and fleet operations without creating another
    65	  authority surface.
    66	
    67	## Store
    68	
    69	The logical layout is:
    70	
    71	```text
    72	<store>/
    73	├── registry.json
    74	└── releases/
    75	    └── v<version>-rc.<n>/
    76	        ├── manifest.json
    77	        ├── standards/
    78	        ├── plugins/spec/
    79	        ├── release/release-note.md
    80	        └── LICENSE
    81	```
    82	
    83	The physical root defaults to the user data directory for the host platform and
    84	may be overridden by `STDO_STORE` or `--store`. Product Definitions never carry
    85	that machine-local path. `stdo://releases/<cut>/...` resolves through the local
    86	registry only after the entry is confined to the expected release directory.
    87	
    88	Installation is staged under the store, verified, made read-only, and renamed
    89	atomically. Existing bytes are never repaired or overwritten in place. A
    90	damaged installation fails closed so the operator can inspect it.
    91	Manager-owned store roots, registries, release directories, payload
    92	directories, and payload files must be physical entries of their declared
    93	type. Verification inventories directories, regular files, redirects, and
    94	special entries without following them; every undeclared entry is damage.
    95	
    96	## Operations
    97	
    98	- `install` names an immutable RC cut directly and changes only the store.
    99	- `sync` installs and verifies the basis already pinned in one definition; it
   100	  never follows the selector and never edits the definition.
   101	- `adopt --dry-run` resolves and reports the exact latest selector target plus a
   102	  digest over current definition bytes, cut, annotated tag, commit, tree, and
   103	  manifest; a lagging selector or same-line downgrade fails closed.
   104	- mutating `adopt` requires that externally accepted digest, re-derives it,
   105	  installs only the bound target, rechecks the definition bytes, then atomically
   106	  changes only `constitution.stdo.basis` and a basis-relative `$schema` URI.
   107	- `bootstrap` owns only one delimited block in each declared agent file and
   108	  preserves all other project bytes exactly. Targets are relative to the
   109	  resolved `product.source_project`; every target is preflighted before writes.
   110	- `fleet` discovers `stdo_<label>.json` files recursively while excluding VCS,
   111	  dependency, generated, and managed-store directories. Every fleet write
   112	  requires `--all`; adoption also requires its aggregate accepted plan digest,
   113	  while bootstrap confines every source project to the fleet root.
   114	
   115	## Refusals
   116	
   117	The manager refuses unannotated or malformed cut identities, lightweight or
   118	lagging version-line selectors, a selector that does not match the highest
   119	published RC, absent or ambiguous matching RC tags, zero or multiple recognized STDO project
   120	layouts, channel downgrades, unaccepted or stale adoption plans, unexpected
   121	manifest digests, damaged or extra installed entries of any type, store or
   122	registry redirection, URI traversal, cross-basis schema locators, invalid
   123	Product Definition shape or formats, bootstrap boundary escape, malformed
   124	markers, and implicit fleet writes.
   125	
   126	## Verification
   127	
   128	The executable boundary is tested against unrelated temporary Git releases for
   129	installation, reinstallation, tamper detection, URI escape, exact-basis sync,
   130	latest-selector adoption, lagging-selector and downgrade refusal, marker
   131	idempotence, fleet discovery, and refusal paths. A
   132	repository dogfood tests independently install the immutable released
   133	`v2.4.3-rc.1` and `v2.5.0-rc.1` cuts and check their known commits, inventories,
   134	canonical aggregate digests, and historical manifest bytes. Synthetic
   135	repository tests also prove the exact `specification_methodology/` monorepo
   136	prefix, repository-root and standards-subtree identities, project-relative
   137	logical members, and refusal of absent or ambiguous layouts. A second dogfood
   138	boundary binds the source Product Definition to the exact installed RC2 builder
   139	basis.

   211	def _schema_path(
   212	    document: dict[str, Any],
   213	    definition_path: Path,
   214	    store: Store,
   215	) -> Path:
   216	    reference = document.get("$schema")
   217	    if not isinstance(reference, str) or not reference:
   218	        raise StdoError(f"Product Definition has no schema locator: {definition_path}")
   219	    parsed = urlparse(reference)
   220	    if parsed.scheme == "stdo":
   221	        return store.resolve(reference)
   222	    if parsed.scheme not in {"", "file"} or parsed.netloc not in {"", "localhost"}:
   223	        raise StdoError(
   224	            f"Product Definition schema must be an installed stdo URI or local file reference: {reference!r}"
   225	        )
   226	    if parsed.query or parsed.fragment:
   227	        raise StdoError(
   228	            f"Product Definition schema locator cannot contain query or fragment: {reference!r}"
   229	        )
   230	    candidate = Path(unquote(parsed.path))
   231	    if not candidate.is_absolute():
   232	        candidate = definition_path.parent / candidate
   233	    candidate = candidate.resolve()
   234	    if not candidate.is_file():
   235	        raise StdoError(f"Product Definition schema does not resolve: {reference!r}")
   236	    return candidate

   239	def validate_definition_document(
   240	    document: dict[str, Any],
   241	    definition_path: Path,
   242	    store: Store,
   243	) -> Path:
   244	    try:
   245	        from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator, FormatChecker
   246	        from jsonschema.exceptions import SchemaError
   247	    except ImportError as exc:
   248	        raise StdoError(
   249	            "Product Definition validation requires the installed stdo-toolchain dependencies"
   250	        ) from exc
   251	
   252	    schema_path = _schema_path(document, definition_path, store)
   253	    schema = load_json(schema_path)
   254	    try:
   255	        Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema)
   256	    except SchemaError as exc:
   257	        raise StdoError(
   258	            f"Invalid Product Definition schema at {schema_path}: {exc.message}"
   259	        ) from exc
   260	    validator = Draft202012Validator(schema, format_checker=FormatChecker())
   261	    errors = sorted(
   262	        validator.iter_errors(document),
   263	        key=lambda item: tuple(str(part) for part in item.absolute_path),
   264	    )
   265	    if errors:
   266	        details: list[str] = []
   267	        for error in errors[:10]:
   268	            location = "/".join(str(part) for part in error.absolute_path) or "<root>"
   269	            details.append(f"{location}: {error.message}")
   270	        if len(errors) > 10:
   271	            details.append(f"... and {len(errors) - 10} more validation errors")
   272	        raise StdoError(
   273	            f"Product Definition fails schema {schema_path}: {'; '.join(details)}"
   274	        )
   275	    return schema_path

   278	def discover_definitions(root: Path | str) -> list[Path]:
   279	    start = Path(root).resolve()
   280	    if start.is_file():
   281	        if not _DEFINITION_NAME_RE.fullmatch(start.name):
   282	            raise StdoError(f"Not an STDO Product Definition filename: {start}")
   283	        return [start]
   284	    if not start.is_dir():
   285	        raise StdoError(f"Product Definition discovery root does not exist: {start}")
   286	    matches: list[Path] = []
   287	    for directory, directories, files in os.walk(start):
   288	        directory_path = Path(directory)
   289	        directories[:] = sorted(
   290	            name
   291	            for name in directories
   292	            if name not in _SKIP_DIRECTORIES
   293	            and not (directory_path / name).is_symlink()
   294	        )
   295	        for filename in sorted(files):
   296	            if _DEFINITION_NAME_RE.fullmatch(filename):
   297	                candidate = directory_path / filename
   298	                if candidate.is_symlink():
   299	                    raise StdoError(
   300	                        f"Product Definition discovery refuses a symlink: {candidate}"
   301	                    )

   304	                    resolved.relative_to(start)
   305	                except ValueError as exc:
   306	                    raise StdoError(
   307	                        f"Product Definition escaped discovery root: {candidate}"
   308	                    ) from exc
   309	                matches.append(resolved)
   310	    return matches

1	# Reference Frame Method
     2	
     3	## Canonical Compression
     4	
     5	A human or computational actor has finite context, finite attention, finite
     6	time, and bounded capability. A material workspace may contain more relevant
     7	truth, history, topology, authority, and evidence than one actor can evaluate
     8	at once.
     9	
    10	The Reference Frame Method makes that limit explicit:
    11	
    12	```text
    13	declared evaluation family
    14	  + exact workspace and topology basis
    15	  + finite material relations and coordinates
    16	  + applicable invariants and authorities
    17	  + admissible evidence and exclusions
    18	  + actor capability envelope
    19	  = activated reference frame
    20	  -> satisfied | falsified | indeterminate | out_of_frame | invalid_basis
    21	```
    22	
    23	A project engages a body of work through a declared frame set:
    24	
    25	```text
    26	workspace and governed outcome
    27	  + accumulated practice and historical failures
    28	  + available actor capabilities
    29	  + human judgment
    30	  -> declared frame set
    31	  -> bounded evaluations
    32	  -> conjunction or translation where required
    33	  -> coverage ledger and residual uncertainty
    34	  -> empirical frame-set revision
    35	```
    36	
    37	The reference frame is the atomic engagement unit. Frame-set selection,
    38	activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage, and revision are
    39	separate method functions. A frame does not need to contain a universal theory
    40	of its possible relationships before it can support a bounded evaluation.
    41	
    42	`Atomic engagement unit` names the unit that can be activated and evaluated as
    43	one bounded context. It does not assert that every relation inside the frame is
    44	one irreducible semantic atom. A frame may carry several semantic atoms and
    45	several owner relations without merging their meaning or authority.
    46	
    47	---
    48	
    49	## Position
    50	
    51	This method governs how finite actors construct and use bounded reasoning or
    52	execution contexts over a changing body of work. It applies to human work,
    53	agentic work, deterministic evaluation, probabilistic construction, assurance,
    54	and mixed work where the governing product or method permits them.
    55	
    56	This is an engagement meta-method. It does not define a domain Product,
    57	specification taxonomy, design ontology, runtime, workflow, or assurance
    58	implementation. An application profile binds this method to a concrete method,
    59	workspace, or Product and declares the evaluations and authorities meaningful
    60	there.
    61	
    62	`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` owns the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context
    63	`urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation` under the selected
    64	complete STDO basis. This standard owns its frame, activation, evaluation,
    65	basis, relation, result, coverage, and qualification concepts. Application
    66	profiles may define specialist frame families inside that context by explicit
    67	reference; a same-spelled Product or runtime carrier is not imported by
    68	proximity or nominal match.
    69	
    70	The method is substrate-neutral. A reference frame may be represented in prose,
    71	structured data, a prompt, a design asset, a typed carrier, a runtime context,
    72	or another form selected by its consumer. No class, aggregate, actor,
    73	controller, service, registry, graph, or frame engine is required.
    74	
    75	---
    76	
    77	## Core Claims
    78	
    79	1. No finite actor is presumed to hold the complete material workspace in
    80	   active attention.
    81	2. A useful frame is finite and sufficient for a declared evaluation family.
    82	3. The evaluations to be made determine the material attention surface.
    83	4. Human authority may declare a practical project frame set from accumulated
    84	   practice without deriving a unique frame partition mechanically.
    85	5. Frames may overlap, compose, refine, restrict, translate, or succeed one
    86	   another. Hierarchy is one optional relation.
    87	6. Several frames may be used together without composing their internal
    88	   coordinate systems.
    89	7. Coverage is relative to a declared workspace, governed outcome, evaluation
    90	   inventory, basis, and time.
    91	8. A frame selection or frame result cannot acquire semantic, operation, or
    92	   decision authority from its breadth, usefulness, actor, or implementation
    93	   technology.
    94	9. Unknown and out-of-frame results are lawful pressure for reconfiguration.
    95	   They are not failed evaluations or implied acceptance.
    96	10. Historical failures, resets, and invisible violations are evidence for
    97	    improving a frame declaration, activation, actor assignment, or frame set.
    98	
    99	---
   100	
   101	## Definitions
   102	
   103	### Evaluation
   104	
   105	An **evaluation** is a declared question whose admissible result family,
   106	evidence basis, decision authority, and operation authority where it performs a
   107	material action are known. An evaluation may ask for a judgment, prediction,
   108	construction, comparison, proof, refusal, classification, or action
   109	recommendation.
   110	
   111	An evaluation family groups questions that require the same material relation
   112	manifold, authority basis, and result algebra. Similar wording does not prove
   113	that two evaluations belong to the same family.
   114	
   115	### Workspace
   116	
   117	A **workspace** is the bounded body of material being reasoned over or acted
   118	upon. It may include constitutional sources, domain assets, designs,
   119	implementations, tools, runtime state, evidence, historical records, external
   120	dependencies, and human decisions.
   121	
   122	The workspace is broader than a repository. A repository is one possible
   123	carrier.
   124	
   125	### Basis
   126	
   127	A **basis** identifies the exact state against which an evaluation is made. It
   128	includes every version, identity, time, topology, authority, configuration, or
   129	evidence coordinate whose change can alter the evaluation.
   130	
   131	A basis may be immutable or moving. A moving basis must declare how advancement
   132	is detected and when reevaluation is required.
   133	
   134	### Material relation
   135	
   136	A relation is **material** to an evaluation when a lawful change to that
   137	relation can change the evaluation result, invalidate its basis, change the
   138	admissible evidence, change who may perform a material operation, or change who
   139	may decide it.
   140	
   141	Materiality is evaluation-relative. A relation may be material in one frame and
   142	irrelevant in another.
   143	
   144	### Material-relation manifold
   145	
   146	The **material-relation manifold** is the finite, jointly interpretable set of
   147	variables, entities, identities, states, relations, invariants, authorities,
   148	observations, and exclusions needed for an evaluation family.
   149	
   150	`Manifold` names a bounded relation space with potentially overlapping
   151	coordinate charts. It does not require geometric mathematics or a runtime
   152	manifold abstraction.
   153	
   154	### Coordinate
   155	
   156	A **coordinate** is the complete local position from which a value, event,
   157	decision, observation, or action is interpreted. It includes the basis,
   158	identity, lineage, input, evidence, and authority information required by the
   159	evaluation.
   160	
   161	Equal names, values, shapes, locations, or apparent topology positions do not
   162	establish coordinate equality. Equality follows a declared relation.
   163	
   164	### Topology
   165	
   166	**Topology** is the relation structure among the material entities,
   167	capabilities, authorities, lifecycle state spaces, adjacencies, and seams
   168	visible to a frame at one basis. The frame need not contain the workspace's
   169	complete topology.
   170	
   171	A state-value change preserves the frame topology only when it preserves every
   172	material entity, relation, lifecycle, authority, capability, adjacency, and
   173	seam. A state transition that changes any such relation is a topology mutation
   174	and may invalidate the frame's coordinates.
   175	
   176	### Evidence
   177	
   178	**Evidence** is the exact observation or artifact admitted for an evaluation.
   179	Evidence carries provenance, subject identity, basis, and scope. Evidence does
   180	not become semantic truth or decision authority merely because it is available
   181	inside a frame.
   182	
   183	### Authority
   184	
   185	The method distinguishes:
   186	
   187	- **frame-set authority**: the human authority that declares or accepts the
   188	  project frame set;
   189	- **semantic authority**: the owner of meaning for a material relation;
   190	- **evaluation authority**: the role permitted to perform an evaluation;
   191	- **operation authority**: the owner-issued grant to construct, transform,
   192	  admit, publish, or mutate a material subject where an evaluation performs
   193	  such an operation;
   194	- **decision authority**: the role permitted to accept, reject, or otherwise
   195	  dispose its result; and
   196	- **actor identity**: the human, agent, tool, or process performing work.
   197	
   198	These relations may coincide in a lawful case. They never collapse by default.
   199	Declaring, selecting, activating, or executing a frame does not grant semantic,
   200	operation, or decision authority. A read-only evaluation declares no operation
   201	authority. An effectful evaluation inherits the exact operation grant from its
   202	existing owner; the frame does not create that grant.
   203	
   204	Human authority may act directly or through an explicitly admitted bounded
   205	proxy where the governing identity and authority law permits it. Proxy identity
   206	and human-authority identity remain distinct.
   207	
   208	### Disjointness And Independence
   209	
   210	Three relations remain distinct:
   211	
   212	- **frame disjointness** is structural: two frames share no material variable,
   213	  coordinate, evidence, or result dependency for the declared evaluations;
   214	- **evaluation independence** is procedural: separately activated evaluations
   215	  do not consume or influence one another's unclosed working results, although
   216	  they may intentionally inspect the same subject, overlap in their manifolds,
   217	  and later supply closed results to a conjunction; and
   218	- **assurance independence** is claim-relative: the governing assurance law
   219	  states the required non-authorship, evidence-acquisition, reference-exposure,
   220	  actor, and configuration separation for a verdict to count as independent
   221	  assurance.
   222	
   223	Disjoint frames need not be independently evaluated, and independently
   224	activated evaluations need not be disjoint. The unqualified word
   225	`independent` does not establish any of these relations by itself.
   226	
   227	### Capability envelope
   228	
   229	A **capability envelope** declares the competence, context capacity, tools,
   230	access, applicable evaluation- or assurance-independence conditions, and
   231	configuration required to activate a frame and perform its evaluations.
   232	
   233	The same frame may be usable by one actor and unusable by another. Actor
   234	capability may justify a different frame size or activation sequence. It cannot
   235	waive an invariant or widen authority.
   236	
   237	### Reference frame
   238	
   239	A **reference frame** is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates,
   240	authority, evidence, and result relations required to perform one declared
   241	evaluation family over a stated basis.
   242	
   243	Formally, a frame may be described as:
   244	
   245	\[
   246	F = \langle Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D \rangle
   247	\]
   248	
   249	where:
   250	
   251	- \(Q\) is the evaluation family;
   252	- \(B\) is the workspace and topology basis;
   253	- \(M\) is the material-relation manifold;
   254	- \(C\) is the coordinate and equality law;
   255	- \(I\) is the applicable invariant set;
   256	- \(A\) is the authority relation;
   257	- \(E\) is the admissible evidence and provenance law;
   258	- \(X\) is the exclusion and prohibited-assumption set;
   259	- \(R\) is the closed result algebra;
   260	- \(J\) is the invalidation and rechart condition;
   261	- \(K\) is the actor capability envelope; and
   262	- \(D\) is the optional set of declared dependencies, overlaps, inputs, and
   263	  outputs involving other frames.
   264	
   265	This tuple specifies the relation. It is not a required schema or runtime
   266	carrier.
   267	
   268	### Activated frame
   269	
   270	An **activated frame** binds one frame declaration to an exact evaluation,
   271	workspace subject, basis, actor, and evidence acquisition boundary. A reusable
   272	frame declaration is not evidence that a particular activation was correct.
   273	
   274	### Frame set
   275	
   276	A **frame set** is the human-declared family of frames available for a governed
   277	outcome or workspace. It may intentionally contain overlaps, alternatives,
   278	specialist frames, broad exploratory frames, and separately activated assurance
   279	frames.
   280	
   281	A frame set is not required to be a partition, tree, stack, or exhaustive
   282	ontology.
   283	
   284	### Active frame configuration
   285	
   286	An **active frame configuration** is the set of frame activations and declared
   287	result relations used for one evaluation or decision. It may contain one frame
   288	or several disjoint, overlapping, or composed frames. Separately activated
   289	evaluations may be disjoint or overlapping.
   290	
   291	### Lens
   292	
   293	A **lens** is a reusable family of questions applied across a frame
   294	configuration. Authority, capability and reuse, temporal behavior, transport,
   295	and proof are examples of lenses when named abstractly.
   296	
   297	A lens becomes a frame only when it is instantiated with a bounded evaluation,
   298	basis, material manifold, evidence, authorities, result algebra, and capability
   299	envelope.
   300	
   301	### Role, persona, abstraction, and component
   302	
   303	A **role** allocates responsibility or authority. A **persona** alters an
   304	actor's approach or salience. An **abstraction** hides or contracts detail. A
   305	**component** is a structural part of a subject.
   306	
   307	Each may help construct or activate a frame. None is a reference frame by
   308	identity alone. One component may appear in several frames, and one frame may
   309	cross several components.
   310	
   311	---
   312	
   313	## Reference Frame Laws
   314	
   315	### RF-001 Evaluation Relativity
   316	
   317	Every frame declares the evaluation family it supports. A frame with no
   318	declared evaluation family has no testable sufficiency boundary.
   319	
   320	### RF-002 Finite Attention
   321	
   322	An activated frame contains a finite attention surface that fits the selected
   323	actor's declared capability envelope. A frame that requires undeclared ambient
   324	memory, conversation history, or an effectively global workspace context is
   325	not reconstructable for that actor.
   326	
   327	### RF-003 Material Sufficiency
   328	
   329	Every known relation whose lawful change can alter the evaluation result,
   330	basis validity, evidence sufficiency, operation authority, or decision
   331	authority appears in the frame or enters through a declared authoritative
   332	input.
   333	
   334	Omitting a material relation makes the frame insufficient. The method does not
   335	require proving that no undiscovered material relation exists.
   336	
   337	### RF-004 Irrelevance Exclusion
   338	
   339	Relations that cannot affect the declared evaluation remain outside active
   340	attention unless they are required to establish irrelevance. A frame does not
   341	expand merely because adjacent workspace material exists.
   342	
   343	### RF-005 Exact Basis And Coordinates
   344	
   345	Every result binds its exact subject, basis, coordinates, and evidence scope.
   346	A stale, advanced, ambiguous, or mismatched basis returns `invalid_basis` or
   347	requires reactivation. Apparent equality does not substitute for declared
   348	coordinate equality.
   349	
   350	### RF-006 Authority Conservation
   351	
   352	A frame carries and applies admitted authority. It does not mint, widen,
   353	transfer, or reconstruct semantic, evaluation, operation, or decision authority
   354	from actor identity, available capability, evidence shape, implementation
   355	reachability, or frame selection.
   356	
   357	### RF-007 Semantic, Evidence, And Verdict Separation
   358	
   359	Semantic law defines what the evaluation means. Evidence supplies observations.
   360	The evaluator applies the declared relation. Where the evaluation performs a
   361	material operation, the existing operation owner supplies the exact grant.
   362	Decision authority disposes the result. A frame declaration keeps these roles
   363	distinguishable even when one actor lawfully performs several of them.
   364	
   365	### RF-008 Overlap Without Identity Collapse
   366	
   367	Frames may share entities, variables, evidence, or coordinates. Shared material
   368	does not establish identical meaning, basis, authority, or result. Every
   369	cross-frame equality or translation used by an evaluation is declared where it
   370	is needed.
   371	
   372	### RF-009 No Assumed Hierarchy
   373	
   374	Frames may relate through disjointness, overlap, refinement, restriction,
   375	translation, temporal succession, composition, or governance. Parent and child
   376	relations apply only where explicitly declared.
   377	
   378	Functional decomposition, authority precedence, frame configuration, subject
   379	topology, and evaluation dependency are distinct relation structures. A
   380	consumer may align them where the governed subject warrants it. It may not
   381	silently treat them as one hierarchy.
   382	
   383	### RF-010 Composition On Demand
   384	
   385	Using several frames does not require composing their internal manifolds.
   386	Composition law is required only when the governing evaluation combines their
   387	internal variables, transports evidence or values across them, or treats their
   388	operations as one material execution relation.
   389	
   390	Independently activated evaluations may instead return closed results to one
   391	declared conjunction or decision rule.
   392	
   393	### RF-011 Topology Mutation And Recharting
   394	
   395	An activated frame declares the topology changes capable of invalidating its
   396	coordinates or materiality judgment. A detected material topology mutation
   397	causes reevaluation, frame revision, or recharting before the previous result
   398	is reused.
   399	
   400	### RF-012 Closed Results
   401	
   402	Every evaluation returns a member of its declared result algebra. The baseline
   403	result family is:
   404	
   405	- `satisfied`: the declared predicate holds on the exact basis;
   406	- `falsified`: a declared counterexample defeats it;
   407	- `indeterminate`: available admissible evidence cannot decide it;
   408	- `out_of_frame`: the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or
   409	  capability; or
   410	- `invalid_basis`: the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation.
   411	
   412	An application profile may refine this algebra while preserving explicit
   413	indeterminate, out-of-frame, and invalid-basis pressure.
   414	
   415	### RF-013 Reconstructable Activation
   416	
   417	A fresh competent actor inside the declared capability envelope can reconstruct
   418	the activated evaluation from the frame declaration, exact subject, basis, and
   419	admissible inputs without undocumented conversational or historical context.

    47	# STDO Compressed Authority
    48	
    49	## Method Identity
    50	
    51	`STDO` is shorthand for its four key method pillars:
    52	
    53	- `S` — Specification (`SPEC_METHOD.md`);
    54	- `T` — Ticketing (`TICKET_METHOD.md`);
    55	- `D` — Design (`DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md`); and
    56	- `O` — Outcome-Driven Development (`ODD_METHOD.md`).
    57	
    58	`ODD` expands to Outcome-Driven Development. The `O` in `STDO` names that
    59	complete ODD pillar.
    60	
    61	This shorthand does not reduce the STDO Product to four files. Consumer
    62	authority remains one complete immutable released STDO cut with its exact
    63	member inventory.
    64	
    65	## Governing Claim
    66	
    67	Specification is constitutional source. Design and realization are subordinate
    68	implementation surfaces. Code, prompts, tests, generated views, dashboards,
    69	archives, and comments are projections or realization proof, not independent
    70	truth.
    71	
    72	Products, applications, modules, graph functions, build tenants, and runtime
    73	surfaces implement constitutional documents; they do not replace them.
    74	
    75	Method vocabulary names normative capabilities and construction relations.
    76	Consumers bind concrete implementations and immutable identities under their
    77	own Product authority. A downstream Product may prove or falsify conformance;
    78	it cannot supply reusable method meaning. Constitutional examples use neutral
    79	capability and authority identities.
    80	
    81	This aggregate carries cross-source decisions that cannot be closed from one
    82	source-specific compression, including the complete T-008 F1-F5 bundle and the
    83	Reference Frame Method/STDO baseline application relation. Source-specific
    84	compressions remain standalone only for decisions owned by their source and
    85	refuse cross-law closure.
    86	
    87	## Authority Flow
    88	
    89	Use the smallest current authority surface that can decide the question:
    90	
    91	`Goals -> Intent -> Product Definition -> Requirements -> Design -> Code -> Events -> Projection -> Delta -> Scenarios -> Gap Analysis -> Repricing`
    92	
    93	When a lower layer needs a change in meaning, re-enter at the smallest upstream
    94	layer that owns the missing truth.
    95	
    96	## Product Definition Overlay
    97	
    98	- Every STDO-defined product has one `stdo_<label>.json` definition per
    99	  distinct current `WHAT`; `stdo_default.json` is the singleton default.
   100	- `product.definition_id` identifies the mutable `WHAT` definition line, not
   101	  any immutable Product or release produced from it. Product and release
   102	  identities remain separate; a fork or independently governed definition
   103	  receives another definition identity.
   104	- The definition locates complete constitutional authorities and entrypoints,
   105	  local axioms/overrides/disambiguations, collective reference-frame bases,
   106	  Intent/Product/specification `WHAT`, common and tenant-local `HOW`,
   107	  Goals/tickets/comments/optional sprints, and explicit product composition.
   108	  It is a locator and relation authority, not a restatement of referenced
   109	  truth.
   110	- `constitution.stdo.source` and its `stdo://channels/<version>` selector are
   111	  transport and mutable discovery inputs. The exact
   112	  `stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/` URI and installed-manifest digest are the
   113	  sole authored operative STDO selection. Additional constitutional sets and
   114	  every reading entrypoint are basis-qualified.
   115	- A constitutionally sufficient document set collectively makes axioms,
   116	  ontology, epistemology, taxonomy, and semantics recoverable. These are
   117	  coverage dimensions, not five assumed documents or directories.
   118	- Each local disambiguation binds the exact term, target bounded context,
   119	  complete material candidate set, one selected member of that set, owning
   120	  carrier and authority, semantic bases, and governed scope. The overlay
   121	  locates the resolution; it does not own or restate the candidate meanings.
   122	- `reference_frame_bases` is non-empty and locates each durable shared project
   123	  frame-basis declaration, its existing admitting authorities, and exact
   124	  governed scope. A ticket or other authorized work instruction binds one
   125	  agent's exact activation from an applicable basis. The Product Definition
   126	  Overlay is neither an actor registry nor a store of temporary active
   127	  configurations.
   128	  A Product or runtime carrier named `Frame` remains `WHAT` or `HOW`; nominal
   129	  overlap does not make it a collective evaluation frame.
   130	- Existing projects bind their current carriers without restructuring. The
   131	  default `specification/`, `build_tenants/`, and `.ai-workspace/` layout

   133	- One shared versioned store may carry many immutable cuts for many projects.

   165	## Bounded-Context Semantic Isolation
   166	
   167	- Term spelling is a label, not context-free concept identity. Resolve each
   168	  material occurrence by term, bounded-context identity, owning authority,
   169	  selected basis, and governed scope.
   170	- An owning document, section, field, operation, or other surface may declare
   171	  context once. Unqualified use is lawful when exactly one concept resolves.

   173	  nominal match, actor familiarity, frequency, or recency cannot choose one.

   194	- Build tenancy is STDO's `WHAT` once, independent `HOW` one-or-many
   195	  realization model. The bound `what` remains singleton constitutional truth;
   196	  `how.build_tenants` locates one or more project-owned realizations beneath
   197	  it.

   199	  release, and lifecycle state. No tenant becomes a second constitution, and
   200	  one tenant's evidence cannot close another tenant's claim.
   201	- `how.build_tenants` canonically records tenant identities and locations.

   205	- Tenant-local truth remains local. Similarity creates a commonization
   206	  candidate, not shared law; promotion to `common/` requires the applicable

   213	- Build tenancy is not a synonym for hosted, runtime, customer, account, or

   216	
   217	## Prime Operating Rules
   218	
   219	- Do not create a second truth surface when a current authority surface exists.
   220	- Keep active constitutional surfaces present-tense.
   221	- Treat generated artifacts and summaries as read models unless admitted as
   222	  source truth by the owning method.
   223	- Missing traceability is a defect.
   224	- Prefer one algebraic primitive plus projections over multiple local decision
   225	  systems.
   226	- When `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD` is adopted for a new or materially changed
   227	  semantic boundary, treat discovered functionality as input to design, not as
   228	  pre-authorized operation identities. Derive a candidate Ontology, complete
   229	  lifecycle and authority, run whole-family Prime, and then accept the Ontology
   230	  before promoting IACS, public operations, schemas, or modules.
   231	- The Ontology is semantic-design authority, not a replacement for target
   232	  architecture or module design. Domain, sequence, state, authority, IACS, and
   233	  public-contract surfaces preserve it; code and tests derive through
   234	  requirements plus accepted design.
   235	- Naming an admitter is not sufficient. State the complete admission relation
   236	  for each consequential entity-transition domain — entity identity,
   237	  predecessor basis, authority scope, candidate family, decision cardinality,
   238	  admission predicate, durable result, supersession law. Singularity attaches to
   239	  the relation, not one actor; quorum, multi-signature, step-up, and proxy are
   240	  lawful when declared. A projection may produce a candidate but confers no
   241	  admission authority, and reconstructed state is not self-authenticating.
   242	- Disposition every equivalent competing path explicitly as a constituent, a
   243	  replica, a replacement, or a deliberately independent realization of the
   244	  admission law. Disposition does not mean deletion; an undisposed equivalent
   245	  path is the defect, not the equivalence itself.

   255	- Direct and every supported composite or nested boundary preserve the same

1	# STDO Reference Frame Baseline
     2	
     3	## Canonical Compression
     4	
     5	`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` defines the finite engagement atom. The selected
     6	complete STDO cut defines specification, design, construction, assessment,
     7	disposition, checkpoint, continuation, identity, and release law. This profile
     8	maps three practical engagement frames onto those existing owners:
     9	
    10	```text
    11	existing project authority
    12	  + selected complete STDO and Reference Frame Method basis
    13	  + exact governed Product or Product-chain outcome and workspace basis
    14	  + known evaluation inventory, dependencies, and residuals
    15	  -> Executive outcome and basis lock
    16	  -> smallest finite dependency-ready activation frontier
    17	  -> independently activated Worker, Reviewer, and specialist evaluations
    18	  -> closed results, Reviewer technical triage, and declared conjunction
    19	  -> Executive priority, boundary effect, disposition, and next bounded action
    20	  -> updated basis, coverage, residuals, and frontier
    21	  -> repeat or stop
    22	```
    23	
    24	The three frames are overlapping evaluation contexts, not a hierarchy or actor
    25	topology. The Worker supplies the candidate subject but never activates the
    26	Reviewer. The Reviewer evaluates but does not implement. The Executive applies
    27	only decision authority already granted by Product, Goals, requirements,
    28	accepted design, ticket, identity, or release law. The Worker carries only the
    29	construction or transformation authority in its admitted intake. No frame gains
    30	admission, publication, mutation, or other operation authority from its label.
    31	
    32	This profile also derives twelve generic specialist-frame families: Product,
    33	Product Composition, Design, Design Component, Public Boundary, Entity,
    34	Operator, Owner, Effect, Reuse/Foundation, Install, and Proof. They separate recurring evaluation
    35	questions that otherwise collapse across constitutional `WHAT`, structural
    36	`HOW`, identity, authority, effects, foundations, installed subjects, and
    37	evidence. They are available frame families, not mandatory actors, stages,
    38	components, services, files, or runtime types. An activation selects only the
    39	families material to its exact evaluation and retains an explicit residual for
    40	any material family it cannot cover.
    41	
    42	This profile also derives four Product-testing specialist-frame families:
    43	user acceptance, end to end, integration, and unit. They are activated inside
    44	the same Executive, Worker, and Reviewer engagement relation; they are not new
    45	roles, stages, authorities, or a testing hierarchy. Their ordinary evidence
    46	topology is:
    47	
    48	```text
    49	Product and accepted design
    50	  |- user-outcome claims -> user-acceptance frames
    51	  |- runnable causal-path claims -> end-to-end frames
    52	  |- composition-boundary claims -> integration frames
    53	  `- module-owned laws -> unit frames
    54	
    55	bound results -> declared conjunction -> Product or release disposition
    56	```
    57	
    58	The fan-out assigns claims to their congruent evidence frames; it is not an
    59	authority hierarchy or a claim that one frame decomposes into another.
    60	Evidence may relate through declared conjunction, translation, falsification,
    61	and re-entry. A broader frame cannot make a module-owned law true, and any
    62	number of narrower green frames cannot establish an unevaluated Product
    63	composition or user outcome.
    64	
    65	A project may adopt this profile or define another reference-frame
    66	configuration. That choice is admitted by the existing project authority that
    67	owns the affected decision. A local axioms file may carry the decision; the file
    68	does not become a new constitutional owner merely by carrying it.

   119	## Empirical Revision Boundary
   120	
   121	Accumulated delivery practice and observed failure may inform frame selection,
   122	qualification, and revision. Such evidence does not become STDO authority and

   217	### Executive
   218	
   219	**Executive** is the profile label for the frame that selects or confirms the
   220	bounded activation configuration and consumes closed Worker and Reviewer
   221	results under existing project decision authority. It holds the complete
   222	Product view and current MVP or release mandate needed to assign priority,
   223	apply disposition, and select the next authorized action.
   224	
   225	It may be occupied by direct human authority or by a bounded proxy admitted
   226	under `STDO-UP-020`, `IDENTITY_METHOD.md`, and the current project authority.
   227	It is not a universal semantic owner, controller, manager service, or runtime
   228	executive observer.
   229	
   230	---
   231	
   232	## Executive Attention, Evaluation, And Action
   233	
   234	Executive is the profile frame for three inseparable duties over one governed
   235	outcome:
   236	
   237	1. **attention management** maintains the exact outcome and basis, Product-role
   238	   map, evaluation inventory, dependency relation, unresolved frontier, actor
   239	   envelopes, current MVP or release mandate, applicable triage policy, and
   240	   residual boundary, then selects the smallest
   241	   dependency-ready activation set sufficient for the next decision within the
   242	   finite actor envelopes;
   243	2. **evaluation orchestration** activates capable Workers, Reviewers, or
   244	   specialists, preserves their exact subjects and bases, and consumes only
   245	   closed results or declared translations; and
   246	3. **authorized action selection** assigns priority, determines the effect on
   247	   the current promotion boundary, applies an existing disposition, and issues
   248	   only the next already-authorized activation or action.
   249	
   250	Executive does not contain the complete workspace, perform every evaluation,
   251	or acquire Product meaning, implementation, mutation, acceptance, publication,
   252	or other operation authority from the role. A material effect remains owned by
   253	the actor carrying its exact operation grant.
   254	
   255	The attention cycle is:
   256	
   257	```text
   258	U0 = every known material evaluation not closed on the current basis
   259	
   260	while U is non-empty:
   261	  select a finite dependency-ready subset M that fits the assigned actors
   262	  activate each member of M against the exact outcome and basis
   263	  keep assurance-independent evaluations free of unclosed peer results
   264	  record every closed result, technical triage, residual, and invalidation condition
   265	  apply only declared conjunctions or translations
   266	  assign priority and boundary effect only under the current Product mandate
   267	  invalidate affected results when the subject or basis changes
   268	  update U from coverage, dependencies, conflicts, and discovered materiality
   269	
   270	stop only when every mandatory evaluation is closed, or governing authority
   271	has explicitly retained every remaining residual consistently with the claim
   272	```
   273	
   274	This relation requires no scheduler or frame engine. `M` may contain parallel
   275	activations. Recursion follows declared evaluation dependencies and bounded
   276	refinements; it does not nest or join undifferentiated copies of every frame.
   277	The Executive retains the frontier and closed-result ledger in attention, not
   278	the undocumented working context of every evaluator.
   279	
   280	Severity supplied by Reviewer is evaluation evidence. Priority, current-boundary
   281	effect, `STDO-UP-020` disposition, and subsequent action are Executive decisions.
   282	They remain distinct ledger entries even when a Product-defined policy maps one
   283	to another.
   284	
   285	Every result returns to Executive, a declared conjunction, or another frame
   286	through an explicit `D` relation. No lateral handoff, child completion, model
   287	response, tool output, or shared actor implicitly activates another frame or
   288	authorizes continuation. A consumer receives the closed result and its source
   289	routes, not the child's hidden reasoning context.
   290	
   291	### Executive Drift Locks
   292	
   293	Before activation and before disposition, Executive revalidates:
   294	
   295	- **outcome lock** — selected Goal, Product outcome, boundary, and lawful
   296	  re-entry class, current MVP or release mandate, and triage policy remain
   297	  unchanged;
   298	- **basis lock** — subject, authority, dependency, configuration, topology,
   299	  evidence, time, and candidate coordinates remain exact and current;
   300	- **Product-role lock** — mutable Source Project, Product Definition,
   301	  Release Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, and dependent Product identities
   302	  remain distinct, and every Development Product role remains bound to its
   303	  exact underlying Install;
   304	- **authority lock** — semantic, evaluation, operation, decision, acceptance,
   305	  and publication owners and grants remain unchanged; and
   306	- **coverage-and-return lock** — every material evaluation and interaction is
   307	  closed or explicit residual, and every consumed result followed its declared
   308	  return relation.
   309	
   310	Changed Product meaning requires re-entry. A stale or substituted basis is
   311	`invalid_basis`. Missing material scope is `out_of_frame`. Missing operation
   312	authority refuses activation or the effect. An unresolved mandatory conflict
   313	prevents a satisfied conjunction. Executive does not repair any of these by
   314	making its own frame larger.
   315	
   316	### Product-Chain Basis
   317	
   318	A governed outcome may concern one Product or an explicit directed chain of
   319	Products. Its basis records the distinct role of every mutable Source Project,
   320	current Product Definition, exact candidate checkpoint, Release Cut, Product,
   321	Install, Artifact, Development Product, dependent Product, and composition
   322	edge. Each Development Product role binds one exact underlying Install
   323	identity. Each edge names its source and target roles, governing authority and
   324	contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary, refusal, and invalidation.
   325	
   326	An installed Product may lawfully build its own successor or another Product.
   327	That Development Product remains distinct from the mutable Source Project and
   328	the Product being authored. Directory nesting, shared code, shared actors,
   329	source imports, tool reachability, matching labels, or output equality creates
   330	no Product identity, composition edge, or authority transfer.
   331	
   332	Exact basis does not make a Source Project immutable. A Worker may
   333	cumulatively mutate the exact Source Project and write territory named by its
   334	operation grant. A Reviewer evaluates an exact candidate checkpoint produced
   335	from that workspace. Repair advances the workspace, creates a new candidate,
   336	and invalidates affected results. A released Product, Release Cut, or exact
   337	Install remains immutable under its own lifecycle law; it does not impose
   338	immutability on the Source Project constructing a successor.
   339	
   340	### Worker
   341	
   342	**Worker** is the profile label for `STDO-UP-020`'s bounded constructor role
   343	when activated as a reference frame. It owns construction and self-review
   344	inside its exact intake through the operation authority inherited from the
   345	governing work relation. It does not acquire admission, publication, acceptance,
   346	or continuation authority.
   347	
   348	### Reviewer
   349	
   350	**Reviewer** is the profile label for the independent live-surface evaluation
   351	consumed by the `STDO-UP-020` assessment relation and governed by
   352	`STDO-UP-007` and `STDO-UP-022` when activated as a reference frame. It
   353	evaluates one exact subject and returns a closed result with evidence-bound
   354	technical triage when a finding exists. It does not implement the repair,
   355	assign priority, apply disposition, or activate the next frame.
   356	
   357	### Technical triage, severity, priority, and boundary effect
   358	
   359	**Technical triage** is the Reviewer-owned assessment of one finding against
   360	the exact evaluated claim and basis. Where supported by admissible evidence and
   361	the actor capability envelope, it records:
   362	
   363	- the affected claim and observed failure;
   364	- severity under the Product-selected severity scale;
   365	- causal assessment and confidence;
   366	- blast radius and affected users, paths, or relations;
   367	- available workaround or containment;
   368	- repair complexity, regression risk, and material dependencies; and
   369	- residual uncertainty and the evidence required to reduce it.
   370	
   371	Missing causal or repair evidence remains explicit. Reviewer returns
   372	`indeterminate` or `out_of_frame` pressure where the missing relation can change
   373	the evaluation; it does not invent precision or send work laterally to Worker.
   374	
   375	**Severity** grades consequence if the finding manifests. **Priority** orders
   376	response relative to the complete Product outcome, likelihood and exposure,
   377	current MVP or release mandate, reversibility, dependencies, cost of delay, and
   378	available capacity. Reviewer grades severity. Executive assigns priority.
   379	
   380	The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis binds the severity scale,
   381	priority scale, current-boundary decision cutoff, and non-waivable hard stops.
   382	This profile imposes no universal numeric scale. Severity, priority, Reference
   383	Frame Method result, and current-boundary effect remain distinct. None alone
   384	makes a finding release-blocking.
   385	
   386	**Current-boundary effect** is Executive's determination that the finding blocks
   387	the current promotion boundary, requires narrowing, or may remain an explicit
   388	residual. Executive then applies exactly one existing `STDO-UP-020`
   389	disposition. A hard stop or falsified mandatory claim cannot be waived by
   390	lowering priority. An observation outside the exact claim boundary cannot
   391	create another review round merely by receiving a severe label.
   392	
   393	### Work result
   394	
   395	A **work result** is the closed Worker-to-Executive output used by this profile.
   396	It exists only after successful Worker activation. An `activation_refusal`
   397	returns directly to Executive and creates neither a Worker activation nor a
   398	Worker result.
   399	
   400	The work-result variants are profile carriers, not new STDO semantic
   401	dispositions. They are disjoint by their accompanying Reference Frame Method
   402	result:
   403	
   404	- `candidate_ready` accompanies `satisfied`: an exact candidate and transition
   405	  evidence are available;
   406	- `refused` accompanies `falsified`: lawful activation occurred, but a
   407	  governing prohibition or owner-valid construction refusal defeats the
   408	  requested construction;
   409	- `incomplete` accompanies `indeterminate`: the valid activation has not
   410	  produced a candidate because admissible evidence or bounded execution cannot
   411	  yet decide or complete the relation; and
   412	- `re_entry_requested` accompanies `out_of_frame` or `invalid_basis`: a
   413	  material decision lies outside Worker authority or the activated basis can no
   414	  longer support the work.
   415	
   416	The mapping is total and exclusive after lawful activation. Payload wording,
   417	stop timing, or actor preference cannot select another variant. A capability,
   418	authority, stale-basis, ambiguous-basis, or topology mismatch known during
   419	activation is an `activation_refusal`, not a synthetic Worker result.
   420	
   421	Consumers choose the representation. `STDO-UP-020` remains the owner of the
   422	execution relation and its semantic dispositions.
   423	
   424	### Exact candidate
   425	
   426	An **exact candidate** is the subject identity required by `STDO-UP-020`
   427	transition evidence and `STDO-UP-007` review traceability. Where
   428	`STDO-UP-022` generic method qualification applies, its construction result is
   429	frozen before material reference exposure as that clause requires. Elsewhere,
   430	this profile stabilizes the review subject through an immutable identity or an
   431	equivalent exact-subject relation sufficient for the claimed assessment.
   432	
   433	This profile does not create a new constitutional lifecycle state named
   434	`frozen`.
   435	
   436	### Baseline-adoption projection
   437	
   438	A **baseline-adoption projection** consumes the Product-owned Project
   439	Reference-Frame Basis defined by
   440	`SPEC_METHOD.md#collective-reference-frame-basis`. Where that basis adopts this
   441	profile, the projection records the selected profile mapping, exact outcome,
   442	actor envelopes, evidence coordinates, and revision conditions needed in
   443	addition to the Product binding. It is not a second frame-basis definition and
   444	does not mint the authority it projects.

   982	## Complete Engagement Transition
   983	
   984	### 1. Existing Authority Selects The Basis
   985	
   986	Goals, Product, requirements, accepted design, ticket, release, or an admitted
   987	bounded proxy selects the outcome and work authority under its existing STDO
   988	owner. The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis projects that decision.
   989	
   990	### 2. Executive Activates Worker
   991	
   992	The Executive applies `REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` activation to the
   993	`STDO-UP-020` sufficient execution intake. The activation identifies:
   994	
   995	- selected complete STDO and project authority;
   996	- exact governed outcome and checkpoint;
   997	- affected causal relation set and governing invariants;
   998	- selected computational relations and specialist frames;
   999	- testing claims, exact subjects, frame topology, material combination
  1000	  populations, ordinary paths, oracles, and forbidden-path exclusions where
  1001	  testing evidence is required;
  1002	- Worker authority, capability envelope, and the exact inherited operation
  1003	  grant, subject, and write territory where mutation is authorized;
  1004	- evidence and qualification obligations;
  1005	- exclusions, prohibited competing paths, stop conditions, and re-entry
  1006	  conditions; and
  1007	- the exact bounded action already authorized.
  1008	
  1009	If activation detects a known capability, authority, subject, basis, or
  1010	topology mismatch, it returns `activation_refusal` directly to Executive. No
  1011	Worker frame is active, no Worker evaluation occurs, and Executive must not
  1012	manufacture a Worker result to represent the failed activation.
  1013	
  1014	### 3. Worker Returns To Executive
  1015	
  1016	Every Worker activation terminates in one closed work result sent to the
  1017	Executive:
  1018	
  1019	```text
  1020	WorkerResult
  1021	  = candidate_ready(exact_subject, transition_evidence, residuals)
  1022	  | refused(reason, authority, evidence)
  1023	  | incomplete(residuals, evidence, stop_basis)
  1024	  | re_entry_requested(owner, material_relation, evidence)
  1025	```
  1026	
  1027	The notation is explanatory and mandates no schema.
  1028	
  1029	Each variant accompanies exactly one Reference Frame Method result under the
  1030	mapping in `Work result`: `satisfied -> candidate_ready`, `falsified ->
  1031	refused`, `indeterminate -> incomplete`, and `out_of_frame | invalid_basis ->
  1032	re_entry_requested`. The mapping applies only after lawful activation.
  1033	
  1034	The Worker does not send a candidate directly into an implicitly active
  1035	Reviewer. It stops after returning the result.
  1036	
  1037	### 4. Executive Evaluates The Work Result
  1038	
  1039	For `refused`, `incomplete`, or `re_entry_requested`, the Executive verifies
  1040	the exact basis and applies the existing authority relation. It records the
  1041	applicable `STDO-UP-020` disposition or reactivates work only when the current
  1042	authority already permits that action. None of these variants can be treated as
  1043	accepted progress merely because work occurred.
  1044	
  1045	For `candidate_ready`, the Executive verifies the exact subject and determines
  1046	whether independent assessment is required by `STDO-UP-007`,
  1047	`STDO-UP-020`, `STDO-UP-022`, Product, release, risk, or the admitted work
  1048	contract. Green aggregate status cannot satisfy this step when a required
  1049	user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration, unit, or negative-path result is
  1050	missing, bound to another subject, or contradicted by a material frame result.
  1051	
  1052	### 5A. Candidate Does Not Require Independent Review
  1053	
  1054	When independent review is not required, the Executive consumes the exact
  1055	candidate, Worker self-review, transition evidence, and any mandatory
  1056	specialist-frame results. It applies `STDO-UP-020` disposition within its
  1057	decision envelope.
  1058	
  1059	Self-review remains Worker evidence. The disposition does not relabel it as
  1060	independent.
  1061	
  1062	### 5B. Candidate Requires Independent Review
  1063	
  1064	When independent review is required, the Executive activates the Reviewer with:
  1065	
  1066	- exact candidate and governing basis;
  1067	- exact claim, composition boundary, population, scope, and exclusions;
  1068	- applicable STDO and project authority;
  1069	- required evidence and ordinary assurance path;
  1070	- required user-acceptance, end-to-end, integration, unit, combinatorial, and
  1071	  negative-path frame results with their exact claims and populations;
  1072	- the Product-selected severity scale and exact affected Product claims;
  1073	- Reviewer capability and independence envelope; and
  1074	- invalidation and stop conditions.
  1075	
  1076	The candidate is frozen before material reference exposure where
  1077	`STDO-UP-022` requires it. Otherwise the subject is stabilized to the exactness
  1078	required by `STDO-UP-007`, `STDO-UP-020`, and the claim.
  1079	
  1080	### 6. Reviewer Returns To Executive
  1081	
  1082	The Reviewer returns one closed evaluation containing:
  1083	
  1084	- frame and activation identity;
  1085	- exact subject, basis, claim, scope, exclusions, and evaluated population;
  1086	- Reviewer actor and independence conditions;
  1087	- evidence and ordinary assurance path acquired;
  1088	- Reference Frame Method result;
  1089	- findings, counterexamples, and adjacent observations;
  1090	- for each finding, affected claim, severity, causal assessment and confidence,
  1091	  blast radius, workaround, repair complexity, regression risk, and residual
  1092	  uncertainty where supportable; and
  1093	- invalidation conditions and re-entry owner where applicable.
  1094	
  1095	### Reviewer Result And Triage Projection
  1096	
  1097	The Reviewer payload projection is total across the Reference Frame Method
  1098	result algebra. `complete`, `indeterminate`, and `not_applicable` below classify
  1099	the finding-level triage payload; they are not new evaluation results,
  1100	dispositions, priorities, or lifecycle states.
  1101	
  1102	| Reference Frame Method result | Finding and triage payload | Executive consumption constraint |
  1103	|---|---|---|
  1104	| `satisfied` | explicit no-finding state; triage `not_applicable`; evidence, residuals, and invalidation remain present | priority and current-boundary effect are `not_applicable` to this review result unless another exact consumed result supplies a finding |
  1105	| `falsified` | one or more exact findings; triage is `complete` where supported and preserves `indeterminate` fields where evidence cannot close them | apply Product-owned priority and boundary policy without mechanically mapping severity to disposition |
  1106	| `indeterminate` | partial finding or observation state; triage `indeterminate`; exact evidence gaps and residual uncertainty | retain uncertainty or reactivate a capable evaluation; do not consume it as satisfaction or a closed finding |
  1107	| `out_of_frame` | the evaluated claim requires an undeclared material relation or evaluator capability; triage `indeterminate`; name the missing relation or capability and exact reconfiguration pressure | refine or reconfigure a capable activation and retain the claim as unresolved; do not consume the result as satisfaction or falsification |
  1108	| `invalid_basis` | basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse result consumption and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |
  1109	
  1110	An adjacent observation outside the evaluated claim does not replace the
  1111	claim-relative result. Reviewer returns it separately with triage
  1112	`not_applicable` to that claim and exact repricing or re-entry pressure. The
  1113	Executive returns it to its declared owner without creating a claim-relative
  1114	block or another review round from severity alone.
  1115	
  1116	The Reviewer returns to Executive, not Worker. It does not edit the candidate,
  1117	direct the repair, or authorize continuation.
  1118	
  1119	### 7. Executive Disposes And Checkpoints
  1120	
  1121	The Executive verifies that every consumed result remains bound to the current
  1122	subject and basis, revalidates the complete Product view and current MVP or
  1123	release mandate, applies any declared result conjunction, assigns priority,
  1124	records the effect on the current promotion boundary, and acts on exactly one
  1125	`STDO-UP-020` disposition within its grant:
  1126	
  1127	- `accept`;
  1128	- `local_repair`;
  1129	- `re_enter`; or
  1130	- `reject`.
  1131	
  1132	`STDO-UP-020` remains the owner of each disposition, exact accepted checkpoint,
  1133	and next already-authorized bounded action. A repair creates a new candidate.
  1134	An affected review is reactivated against that candidate. Acceptance does not
  1135	widen the Product outcome or authorize an unselected successor.
  1136	
  1137	Severity does not mechanically select priority or block promotion. Priority
  1138	does not erase severity or waive a hard stop. The Executive determines blocking
  1139	from the exact affected claim, current mandate, applicable hard stops, and
  1140	Product-owned cutoff policy. An unsupported technical assessment is returned
  1141	through a new or refined activation rather than silently rewritten.
  1142	
  1143	### Executive Promotion Constraint Projection
  1144	
  1145	| Consumed condition | Required Executive constraint |
  1146	|---|---|
  1147	| valid falsification of a mandatory claim governed by a non-waivable hard stop | current promotion boundary blocks regardless of assigned priority or decision cutoff |
  1148	| valid finding below the Product-owned decision cutoff with no hard stop | no mechanical block follows; apply the Product-owned policy and retain any accepted residual explicitly |
  1149	| observation outside the exact evaluated claim | treat as bounded repricing or re-entry input; do not create a claim-relative block or another review round by severity label |
  1150	| unsupported or materially incomplete technical assessment | reactivate a capable evaluation or retain `indeterminate`; do not rewrite Reviewer evidence |

  1336	## Profile Qualification
  1337	
  1338	Qualification of this derived profile applies `REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md`
  1339	Frame Qualification and `STDO-UP-022`; it does not create another qualification
  1340	protocol.
  1341	
  1342	The profile trial evaluates both this profile and its declared composition with
  1343	the exact Reference Frame Method basis without reproducing either as peer
  1344	authority. A valid pure-method trial does not prove this profile, and a valid
  1345	profile trial does not prove the method's complete function population.
  1346	
  1347	Mechanical document checks may protect exact table shape, result cardinality,
  1348	source-digest congruence, and named refusal boundaries. They do not establish
  1349	semantic truth or replace a capable source-linked Reviewer evaluation. Profile
  1350	qualification binds both kinds of evidence without claiming one as the other.
  1351

  1353	
  1354	1. existing project authority selects and projects the frame configuration;
  1355	2. a known incapable or unauthorized actor produces an activation refusal and
  1356	   no Worker result;
  1357	3. a fresh capable Worker reconstructs its intake without hidden conversation
  1358	   history;

  1360	   grant, subject, and write territory; an in-territory mutation succeeds only

  1374	11. missing-frame pressure triggers bounded diagnosis or lawful re-entry;

  1470	
  1471	| Observation | First diagnosis |
  1472	|---|---|
  1473	| implementation produces a coherent capability that is not the selected Product | Product-frame falsification and Product re-entry |
  1474	| a Development Product's structure becomes the authored Product's meaning | Product-role or composition-basis drift |
  1475	| an authorized mutable Source Project is treated as one immutable review subject throughout construction | Source Project and candidate-checkpoint lifecycle collapse |
  1476	| one actor receives every specialist concern as one global context and repeatedly misses known violations | attention-surface or capability mismatch; refine and independently activate frames |

  1479	| a compression, summary, generated map, or prior result replaces current source authority | invalid basis or evidence substitution |

  1488	| one sunny end-to-end path is reported as combinatorial coverage | undeclared interaction population and residual higher-order combinations |

  1506	## Anti-Patterns
  1507	
  1508	This profile is misapplied when:
  1509	
  1510	1. Executive, Worker, or Reviewer is treated as a persona without a declared
  1511	   evaluation and authority relation;
  1512	2. the frames are treated as an organizational hierarchy;
  1513	3. Executive is made a universal context, semantic interpreter, or
  1514	   implementation controller;
  1515	4. Worker sends a candidate directly into an implied Reviewer activation;
  1516	5. an activation refusal is relabeled as a Worker result or any Worker result
  1517	   variant is selected without its required Reference Frame Method result;
  1518	6. refused, incomplete, or re-entry work results have no route to Executive;
  1519	7. Worker accepts its own result, infers continuation, or treats its role label
  1520	   or broad workspace access as mutation authority;
  1521	8. Reviewer relies on Worker narrative instead of acquiring the material live
  1522	   subject;
  1523	9. Reviewer trusts tests without reviewing their semantics where they can
  1524	   change the proof;
  1525	10. Reviewer edits or directs repair while retaining independent-review status;
  1526	11. changed candidate or basis reuses the predecessor verdict;
  1527	12. results from different coordinates are flattened into one relation;
  1528	13. a local axioms file is treated as authority without an owning
  1529	    Goals/Product/requirement/design decision;
  1530	14. this profile restates `STDO-UP-020`, `STDO-UP-007`, or `STDO-UP-022` as
  1531	    peer constitutional law;
  1532	15. a project-defined configuration silently changes selected STDO law;
  1533	16. consumer-specific realization machinery or a renamed architectural
  1534	    equivalent is presented as a universal requirement;
  1535	17. test labels or runner choice substitute for declaring the exact testing
  1536	    frame, subject, claim, population, oracle, path, and falsification condition;
  1537	18. unit-test, assertion, snapshot, line, branch, or function count is used as a
  1538	    Product-confidence or closure measure;
  1539	19. implementation-shaped unit tests are treated as independent design,
  1540	    architecture, integration, installed, or user-outcome assurance;

     2	
     3	## Canonical Compression
     4	
     5	A human or computational actor has finite context, finite attention, finite
     6	time, and bounded capability. A material workspace may contain more relevant
     7	truth, history, topology, authority, and evidence than one actor can evaluate
     8	at once.
     9	
    10	The Reference Frame Method makes that limit explicit:
    11	
    12	```text
    13	declared evaluation family
    14	  + exact workspace and topology basis
    15	  + finite material relations and coordinates
    16	  + applicable invariants and authorities
    17	  + admissible evidence and exclusions
    18	  + actor capability envelope
    19	  = activated reference frame
    20	  -> satisfied | falsified | indeterminate | out_of_frame | invalid_basis
    21	```
    22	
    23	A project engages a body of work through a declared frame set:
    24	
    25	```text
    26	workspace and governed outcome
    27	  + accumulated practice and historical failures
    28	  + available actor capabilities
    29	  + human judgment
    30	  -> declared frame set
    31	  -> bounded evaluations
    32	  -> conjunction or translation where required
    33	  -> coverage ledger and residual uncertainty
    34	  -> empirical frame-set revision
    35	```
    36	
    37	The reference frame is the atomic engagement unit. Frame-set selection,
    38	activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage, and revision are
    39	separate method functions. A frame does not need to contain a universal theory
    40	of its possible relationships before it can support a bounded evaluation.
    41	
    42	`Atomic engagement unit` names the unit that can be activated and evaluated as
    43	one bounded context. It does not assert that every relation inside the frame is
    44	one irreducible semantic atom. A frame may carry several semantic atoms and
    45	several owner relations without merging their meaning or authority.

    49	## Position
    50	
    51	This method governs how finite actors construct and use bounded reasoning or
    52	execution contexts over a changing body of work. It applies to human work,
    53	agentic work, deterministic evaluation, probabilistic construction, assurance,
    54	and mixed work where the governing product or method permits them.
    55	
    56	This is an engagement meta-method. It does not define an application profile,
    57	role mapping, Product-owned frame-basis binding, domain Product, specification
    58	taxonomy, design ontology, runtime, workflow, adoption relation, or assurance
    59	implementation. External methods and Products may import or specialize these
    60	relations under their own authority. That external relation does not enter or
    61	amend the principles.
    62	
    63	`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` owns the reference-frame-evaluation bounded context
    64	`urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation` under its exact
    65	publication basis. This standard owns only its frame declaration, activation,
    66	evaluation, basis, relation, result, coverage, revision, and qualification
    67	concepts. A same-spelled profile, Product, role, or runtime carrier is not
    68	imported by proximity or nominal match.
    69	
    70	The method is substrate-neutral. A reference frame may be represented in prose,
    71	structured data, a prompt, a design asset, a typed carrier, a runtime context,
    72	or another form selected by its consumer. No class, aggregate, actor,
    73	controller, service, registry, graph, or frame engine is required.

    77	## Core Claims
    78	
    79	1. No finite actor is presumed to hold the complete material workspace in
    80	   active attention.
    81	2. A useful frame is finite and sufficient for a declared evaluation family.
    82	3. The evaluations to be made determine the material attention surface.
    83	4. Human authority may declare a practical project frame set from accumulated
    84	   practice without deriving a unique frame partition mechanically.
    85	5. Frames may overlap, compose, refine, restrict, translate, or succeed one
